fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. The LORD says, “No one may go up with you…” (Exodus 34:3). So no helpers join the climb. It's just Moses and the two tablets in his hands. Me, I'd want a buddy just to carry the cookie boxes.

That's the one. The LORD says, “…not even the flocks or herds may graze in front of the mountain.” (Exodus 34:3). So the sheep and cattle don't get to graze in that spot. Even the flocks and herds get told to find another place.

The verse doesn't say that. The LORD says no one may be seen anywhere on the mountain, and not even the flocks or herds may graze in front of it (Exodus 34:3). Camping isn't part of that instruction. Nobody is told to set up tents there.

No whirlwind in this scene. The text says, “And the LORD descended in a cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed His name, the LORD.” (Exodus 34:5). A whirlwind never shows up in the verse. It's a cloud, and He stands with Moses.

Right on target. The LORD calls Himself “…compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness…” (Exodus 34:6). Slow to anger, and abounding in loving devotion. My patience gets tested when the oven timer beeps for the fifth time, and He's out here abounding.
That's right, baker. The LORD says He is “…maintaining loving devotion to a thousand generations…” (Exodus 34:7). A thousand generations. I can't even keep track of one batch on a busy day.

The LORD says the opposite. He says, “…you must tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and chop down their Asherah poles.” (Exodus 34:13). The command is tear down, smash and chop. Leaving them standing isn't on the list.
That's right. The LORD says, “You shall make no molten gods for yourselves.” (Exodus 34:17). One sentence, and no fine print. No loophole for a small one to keep on the shelf.

That's right, baker. The text says, “So Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights…” (Exodus 34:28). The text adds that he went without eating bread or drinking water the whole time. I get dizzy if I skip one cookie break.

Seven's a fine number, friend, but not this time. The text says, “So Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights…” (Exodus 34:28). Seven days is one week. Forty days and forty nights is five of those weeks and then some.

Three days barely covers a long weekend. The text says, “So Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights…” (Exodus 34:28). Forty days and forty nights is more than thirteen of those three-day stretches.
Not quite, baker. The text says Moses “…was unaware that his face had become radiant…” (Exodus 34:29). He had no idea. It's like having flour on your nose and not knowing it.

Yes, baker. The text says Moses “…was unaware that his face had become radiant from speaking with the LORD.” (Exodus 34:29). He had no idea. Aaron and all the Israelites looked at him and saw that his face was radiant (Exodus 34:30).

That's not what happened. Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and all the Israelites “…were afraid to approach him.” (Exodus 34:30). So they held back instead of rushing up. They saw the radiant face and kept their distance.
Yes, baker. Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and all the Israelites looked at Moses and “…were afraid to approach him.” (Exodus 34:30). So nobody rushed up. They stayed back.

Yes, baker. The text says, “And after this all the Israelites came near…” (Exodus 34:32). Earlier they were afraid to approach him (Exodus 34:30), and now they're standing right there. From scared to front row.

Waiting for Aaron isn't mentioned. Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), is already there, since he returned with the leaders (Exodus 34:31). Moses commands them “…to do everything that the LORD had told him on Mount Sinai.” (Exodus 34:32). That's the job.
